investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T04:33:10Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota enforcement condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 because the org-scoped remote agent quota (limit: 100) was already at capacity at the time of the eval run. Because agent creation failed immediately (latencyMs=1268), the runner branch in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1334–1339) never progressed past createAgent(), leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated and causing the contract validation to fail completely. All three remote-agents checks share the same createAgent() call path and received the identical 409 response, confirming a shared upstream dependency failure at the agent-creation layer rather than isolated failures in state or runtime probes.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents failed with 409 — error body contains 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the API enforced a hard quota ceiling.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1268 — the request returned almost immediately, consistent with a quota-gate rejection before any VM provisioning occurred.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — zero evidence fields were written, meaning the runner never reached the post-creation evidence-collection steps.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the probe aborting at createAgent().

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both carry the identical 409 message (sameMessage=true), indicating all three checks hit the same quota wall via the shared createAgent() dependency.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1331-1339: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId(); a 409 at this call would prevent any subsequent evidence writes.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because creation failed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-scoped remote agent quota at capacity: The production org used by the eval service account has reached the swarm backend's hard limit of 100 remote agents. Prior eval runs or real user activity may have accumulated agents that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota before this run.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned remote agents that count against the quota: The runner wraps agent creation in withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs:1337), but if a previous run crashed or was interrupted before cleanup, agents may have been left registered and counted against the limit.

TERTIARY — Eval service account org is shared with real user traffic or other eval pipelines, causing quota contention: If multiple eval workflows or real users share the same org, concurrent agent creation could push the count to the limit independently of eval cleanup behavior.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit dd42aa3 inadvertently affected eval runner behavior: dd42aa3 touched infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs and related files ~18 minutes before the failure, but its subject ('align desktop generation stream timeouts') and touched paths (CI workflow files, not agent creation logic) do not match the 409 quota error. This is a low-confidence hypothesis with no supporting eval or source evidence linking it to the quota condition.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T04:33:10Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a successful agent creation response, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota enforcement condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with HTTP 409 because the org-scoped remote agent quota (limit: 100) was already at capacity at the time of the eval run. Because agent creation failed immediately (latencyMs=1268), the runner branch in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1334–1339) never progressed past createAgent(), leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated and causing the contract validation to fail completely. All three remote-agents checks share the same createAgent() call path and received the identical 409 response, confirming a shared upstream dependency failure at the agent-creation layer rather than isolated failures in state or runtime probes.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1268 — the request returned almost immediately, consistent with a quota-gate rejection before any VM provisioning occurred.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — zero evidence fields were written, meaning the runner never reached the post-creation evidence-collection steps.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because creation failed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-scoped remote agent quota at capacity: The production org used by the eval service account has reached the swarm backend's hard limit of 100 remote agents. Prior eval runs or real user activity may have accumulated agents that were not cleaned up, exhausting the quota before this run.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned remote agents that count against the quota: The runner wraps agent creation in withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs:1337), but if a previous run crashed or was interrupted before cleanup, agents may have been left registered and counted against the limit.

TERTIARY — Eval service account org is shared with real user traffic or other eval pipelines, causing quota contention: If multiple eval workflows or real users share the same org, concurrent agent creation could push the count to the limit independently of eval cleanup behavior.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit dd42aa3 inadvertently affected eval runner behavior: dd42aa3 touched infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs and related files ~18 minutes before the failure, but its subject ('align desktop generation stream timeouts') and touched paths (CI workflow files, not agent creation logic) do not match the 409 quota error. investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime returned a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error with a 404 on the harness endpoint, causing the SSE stream to emit a generation_error frame instead of generation_completed, and no image URL was produced. This is an eval-layer failure localized to the production-api runtime environment's agent harness reachability; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The eval probe called /api/generate/image/stream (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1438) and received a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error with error code 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable or returned an incompatible response at the time of the eval run. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, and imageUrlPresent remained false, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json, lines 271–272). The root cause is uncertain between two possibilities: (1) the agent harness backing the production-api runtime environment was not deployed, misconfigured, or temporarily unavailable at eval time, or (2) the SWARM_BASE_URL / LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable was absent or pointed to a wrong endpoint in the eval runner's execution context. The check is marked required=false with statusImpact=informational for production-api, so this does not constitute a declared outage.
